title: Core Training
summary:
The core is the group of muscles stabilizing the trunk: abdominals, lower back, pelvis, hips, pelvic floor and diaphragm. In pregnancy, core training is not about traditional abs but about strengthening the body's supporting structure to improve function, reduce discomfort, prepare for childbirth and aid postpartum recovery. The transversus abdominis and pelvic floor are key for preventing or managing diastasis recti.

The chapter covers benefits (posture, back and pelvic pain, pelvic floor and pressure control, well-being), four exercise types (deep activation, stabilizing, dynamic, and water), and what to avoid, such as crunches, sit-ups and abdominal doming or coning. It gives frequency, intensity and a 15-20 minute session structure, trimester adaptations, and advice to integrate core work into a multicomponent program.
points: Include 10 min of core exercises in each session, progressing from isometric to dynamic using a resistance band or Swiss ball.
Deep core activation uses transverse abdominis and pelvic floor contraction held 5-10 s, with diaphragmatic breathing: inhale relaxing, exhale while activating.
Modified plank is held 20-30 s and modified side plank 15-20 s per side, starting at 10-15 s if needed.
Avoid sit-ups, crunches and V-ups, which risk coning, higher intra-abdominal pressure and greater rectus separation.
Avoid more than 10 min of uninterrupted supine position from the second trimester onward because of vena cava compression.
Recommended frequency is two to three core sessions per week, 10-20 min each, at moderate RPE 12-14.
A 15-20 min session has warm-up (3-5 min), deep activation (5 min), postural stability (5-7 min), dynamic work (5-7 min) and cool-down (2-3 min).
In the third trimester reduce repetitions, use supports, lengthen rests, and prioritize stability over intensity.
A typical week could be two strength sessions including core, two moderate aerobic sessions, one to two pure core sessions, and daily mobility.
takeaways: Train the deep core (transversus abdominis, pelvic floor, diaphragm) rather than doing sit-ups.
Coordinate breathing with contraction: exhale while activating.
Make planks easier by using knees or an elevated support and shorter holds.
Use supports and a wide, non-slip base for dynamic moves like Pallof press and modified dead bug.
Fit core work inside a multicomponent program of strength, aerobic and mobility.
cautions: If abdominal doming or coning appears, modify or stop the exercise.
Avoid prolonged supine positions from the second trimester onward and rapid or large trunk twisting without stability.
Modify exercises if diastasis recti or other contraindications exist, and avoid excessive abdominal pressure.
